主要内容: Argentina has reached an impasse with its creditors over debt restructuring talks, with both sides accusing each other of refusing to compromise. The government stated it could not "responsibly commit" to the terms offered by creditors, which it claimed were "largely inconsistent with the debt sustainability framework" needed for macroeconomic stability. This could leave around $65 billion in bonds in default for an extended period. The "Ad Hoc" bondholder group, consisting of 13 international asset managers, accused the government of "walking away" from a "comprehensive and sustainable debt restructuring offer." Talks had been ongoing since six months into President Alberto Fernandez's administration, amid a severe economic crisis exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic. Argentina's economy, already in a two-year recession, has been further strained by the health crisis, with over 35,552 confirmed cases and 913 deaths as of May 2020. The government and creditors had been scrambling to reach a deal before a June 19 deadline, though the country is already in default. The negotiations have been complicated by divergent investor demands and the need for a sustainable solution to restore economic stability.
